component.name: FujiNet Go Astrocade (KDE)
component.summary: Self-contained Bally Astrocade with built-in FujiNet

description.p: A Bally Astrocade with FujiNet built in: boots straight into FujiNet's config client, with a clickable keypad window standing in for the console's 24-key keypad so every key can be driven with a mouse.

Emulation is a MAME-derived Astrocade core (the Z80 CPU, the data-chip video with its magic function generator, and the custom I/O sound chip), with FujiNet attached over Bus-Over-IP (BoIP) on loopback TCP. Built-in, searchable Help covers all of it. This is the Qt build.

screenshot.caption: FujiNet CONFIG running on the emulated Astrocade
The debugger FujiNet tab: every FujiBus packet, live
Preferences: system ROM, RAM expansion and ROMs

description.p: Fixed: the macOS app crashed when quitting (Cmd-Q or closing the window) while FujiNet was running.

Video chip tab rebuilt. Display shows the last finished frame as the screen drew it, Decoded redraws screen RAM through the registers each line was drawn with (so games that change colours, the colour boundary or VERBL mid-frame look right), Beam shows this frame up to the beam, and Values shows the raw pens. Zoom to 16x, overlays for the grid, colour boundary, VERBL, interrupt line, beam and recent writes, and a pixel inspector with Break on writes. Registers are decoded with changes highlighted, Colours shows the eight colour registers and the 256 reachable pens with usage counts, and Lines lists where the colours change. Fixed: the Screen RAM picture used the wrong colour set and was garbled in low-res on Windows.

Debugger: ten tabs, with the registers in a strip under all of them. New Watches tab (addresses, labels, ranges; Break on Change), memory search for hex or text, Go To that takes ranges and highlights them, a Cart & I/O tab with the cartridge's image, banks and memory map, Trace and History tabs that record every instruction (with branch and range filters), and Pop Out, which moves any tab into a window of its own. Breakpoint conditions can use old, the byte a write replaced; the Breakpoints tab says why the machine stopped and can clear hit counts; every stop brings the disassembly back to the PC.
Built-in, searchable Help: Help menu (Ctrl+Shift+H, ⌘? on a Mac) and Help buttons in Preferences, the debugger and the console log open the topic for what they show.

A Controllers window in every frontend: the console keypad and all four hand controllers, each with a stick, a trigger and a knob dial. Map any key, gamepad button or stick to any control, the knob included. Any USB or Bluetooth gamepad or joystick now attaches, even one the system has no mapping for, such as an Astro-daptor. Keys are read by physical key, so NumLock and Shift no longer matter.

A new debugger with the same tabs and keys as the other FujiNet Go consoles: execute, read, write and port breakpoints with conditions, editable registers, a console, symbols and an instruction trace. Preferences can import several BIOS files at once. Fixes a hang when the machine restarted while the debugger had it stopped.

Lower CPU use: the picture is drawn on the GPU (with a software fallback) only when the emulator has a new frame, and the display stops updating while the window is hidden. The built-in FujiNet wakes about a tenth as often when nothing is happening. Needs Qt 6.7 or newer.
New: use an external FujiNet. A switch in Preferences makes the app connect to another FujiNet instance at a host:port you enter (for example 127.0.0.1:11500) instead of starting the built-in one.
The Flatpak bundles now name Flathub as their runtime repository, so a downloaded bundle can fetch the GNOME or KDE runtime on a machine that has not set up Flathub.
The Flatpak builds on the GNOME 51 runtime. The software-centre listing now credits FujiNet as developer, declares the app icon, and shows a full set of screenshots for each frontend.

Importing the BIOS now works as in FujiNet Go MS-DOS: a No Astrocade BIOS page until one is imported; Import BIOS and Import BIOS from a Folder take single images, a zip such as MAME's astrocde set, or a folder, and recognise the BIOS by its checksum; Preferences gains a ROMs page; and the machine boots whichever BIOS is imported if the selected one isn't.

Windows: the picture is drawn with Direct3D 11 at the display's refresh, with no flicker; the machine keeps exact 60 Hz time; the debugger has Z80, Video chip and FujiNet tabs laid out to fit the window, with views that keep their place; the FujiNet console log shows the runtime's output; the keypad fits its buttons and shows its arrow keys; Preferences is new.
Debugger: a FujiNet tab shows every FujiBus packet between the Astrocade and FujiNet, both ways, with hex.

Updated FujiNet CONFIG: all text now fits the Astrocade's 8-pixel font, and long footers no longer spill onto the line below and corrupt the current path. Also picks up the latest FujiNet Astrocade cartridge firmware.

Gamepad and keyboard input: a bundled community controller mapping database so more Bluetooth/USB pads are recognized, and keyboard bindings for the hand controller (arrow keys to move, Space to fire) for play without a gamepad, both remappable from the keypad window's Map mode.
First release: the emulator core (validated pixel-exact against MAME) and its FujiNet cartridge, the Qt frontend with the keypad window and debugger, and system-ROM import.
